title: Marketing Foundations
content: Marketing identifies, creates, communicates, and delivers value profitably. It's not just promotion — it's understanding needs deeply. KEY CONCEPTS: Right product, right people, right message, right time and price. WORKED EXAMPLE: A brand wins by solving a specific frustration competitors ignore. PRACTICE: 1) Define your customer's core need. 2) State your value in one sentence. 3) Name who it's NOT for.

title: The 4 Ps
content: Marketing mix: Product, Price, Place, Promotion (plus People, Process, Physical evidence for services). KEY CONCEPTS: Pricing strategies — value-based, penetration, skimming. Place = where/how customers buy. WORKED EXAMPLE: A premium product uses skimming pricing and selective distribution to signal quality. PRACTICE: 1) Define each of your 4 Ps. 2) Pick a pricing strategy. 3) Choose your channels.

title: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning
content: STP: segment the market, target the best-fit segments, position distinctly. Positioning is the key strategic decision. KEY CONCEPTS: Segment by demographic, psychographic, behavioral. Own a clear space in the mind. WORKED EXAMPLE: A brand targets 'busy parents' and positions as 'the 5-minute solution.' PRACTICE: 1) Define 3 segments. 2) Pick your target. 3) Write your positioning statement.

title: Customer Journey & Funnel
content: Journey: Awareness, Consideration, Decision, Retention, Advocacy. Funnel: TOFU/MOFU/BOFU maps content to stage. KEY CONCEPTS: Jobs-to-be-done — customers 'hire' products for progress. Match content to journey stage. WORKED EXAMPLE: Top-funnel education content builds trust before a bottom-funnel demo offer. PRACTICE: 1) Map your customer journey. 2) Assign content to each stage. 3) Find the biggest drop-off.

title: Brand & Positioning
content: A brand is the sum of perceptions — the promise you keep. Brand equity (awareness, associations, loyalty, quality) is a durable asset. KEY CONCEPTS: Strong brands command premiums and cut acquisition cost. Consistency builds brand. WORKED EXAMPLE: A consistent voice across every touchpoint makes a brand instantly recognizable. PRACTICE: 1) State your brand promise. 2) List your brand associations. 3) Audit consistency.

title: Digital Marketing & Metrics
content: Channels: SEO, SEM/PPC, content, social, email (highest ROI), influencer. Metrics: CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC (target 3:1+), ROAS, churn. KEY CONCEPTS: Marketing must tie to revenue. Vanity metrics mislead. WORKED EXAMPLE: Shifting budget to a 5:1 LTV:CAC channel scales profit. PRACTICE: 1) Calculate your CAC and LTV. 2) Find your best channel by ROI. 3) Cut a vanity metric.

title: Grandmaster — Growth Engines
content: Build inbound flywheels: attract, engage, delight → customers become promoters who fuel growth. KEY CONCEPTS: Content builds authority and organic reach. The flywheel compounds; funnels leak. WORKED EXAMPLE: A company's free tool attracts users who refer others, lowering CAC over time. PRACTICE: 1) Design a flywheel loop. 2) Identify your compounding asset. 3) Plan a referral mechanism.

title: King Level — Category Design
content: At King level you build category-defining brands. KEY CONCEPTS: Create and name the category you lead. Shape how the market perceives its own needs. Movements beat campaigns. WORKED EXAMPLE: A company coins a new category term and becomes synonymous with it, owning the space. PRACTICE: 1) Name a category you could own. 2) Define the problem only you frame. 3) Design a movement, not a campaign.
